RaMP multi-database ORA identifies tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:map00350) at rank 7 with FDR 1.18e-06, driven by three input metabolites mapping to the SMPDB tyrosine-pathway cluster. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis returns tyrosine metabolism as its top hit (p = 2.52e-04) with an exceptional 12/12 compound overlap — every member of the mummichog network module matched a query compound. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: disruption of tyrosine metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:map00350) at rank 7 with FDR 1.18e-06, driven by three input metabolites mapping to the SMPDB tyrosine-pathway cluster. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis returns tyrosine metabolism as its top hit (p = 2.52e-04) with an exceptional 12/12 compound overlap — every member of the mummichog network module matched a query compound. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00350) as the top-ranked pathway (p = 0.0131) with 2-methoxytyramine and tyramine as the hitting metabolites. The cross-paradigm consensus is unambiguous: this is a tyrosine-metabolism signal, not a mixed background hit. The driver metabolites are tyramine (KEGG:C00483), pyrocatechol (KEGG:C15571, resolved as catechol in the enrichment output), and 3-methoxytyramine (KEGG:C05587), all of which are confirmed members of the KEGG hsa00350 pathway via the metabolites_hit rosters. Baicalin (KEGG:C10025) appears only as a peripheral RaMP hit with no pathway-level significance. Isopentenyl pyrophosphate (KEGG:C00129) surfaces in the N-glycan biosynthesis and squalene/cholesterol biosynthesis mummichog results, consistent with its role in prenyl diphosphate biochemistry, but its signal strength is secondary to the tyrosine-metabolism winner. Glycerol (KEGG:C00116) contributes to transport and lipid-related peripheral pathways (aquaporin transport, glycerophospholipid metabolism) that appear only in lower-ranked RaMP results. The convergent signal across ORA (hypergeometric), m/z-direct network activity, and KEGG PSEA — three distinct statistical paradigms — establishes tyrosine metabolism as the primary affected pathway in this treatment-versus-control comparison.
